ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A closed box with a square base is to be wrapped with a square sheet of wrapping paper. The box is centered on the wrapping paper with the vertices of the base lying on the midlines of the square sheet of paper, as shown in the figure on the left. The four corners of the wrapping paper are to be folded up over the sides and brought together to meet at the center of the top of the box, point $A$ in the figure on the right. The box has base length $w$ and height $h$. What is the area of the sheet of wrapping paper?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The left figure is a square piece of wrapping paper, inside which a square box bottom, rotated to be displayed as a diamond, is placed centered; the four vertices of the box bottom fall on the horizontal and vertical centerlines of the wrapping paper, and the side length of the box bottom is labeled w. The right figure shows the top view/schematic diagram of the diamond shape formed after folding up, with the four paper corners meeting at the center point A of the top of the box. Reasoning: Looking at the wrapping paper unfolded along one complete diagonal, this diagonal goes from one paper corner to the opposite paper corner, passes through the center of the box bottom, and passes through the box bottom at the midpoints of two opposite sides of the box bottom. Therefore this cross-sectional path after folding is: from the top center A, go w/2 along the box top, after reaching the box edge go downward a height h, go along the box bottom a width w, then go upward along the other side h, and finally go w/2 along the box top back to the top center A. So the diagonal length of the wrapping paper D = w/2 + h + w + h + w/2 = 2(w+h). The area of a square equals half the square of its diagonal, so area = D^2/2 = [2(w+h)]^2/2 = 2(w+h)^2.

method.method_draft: Use the full diagonal of the paper as an unfolded cross-section. One corner of the wrapping paper is labeled A, and the dashed lines indicate fold lines. The right figure shows the top view/schematic diagram of the diamond shape formed after folding up, with the four paper corners meeting at the center point A of the top of the box. Reasoning: Looking at the wrapping paper unfolded along one complete diagonal, this diagonal goes from one paper corner to the opposite paper corner, passes through the center of the box bottom, and passes through the box bottom at the midpoints of two opposite sides of the box bottom. Therefore this cross-sectional path after folding is: from the top center A, go w/2 along the box top, after reaching the box edge go downward a height h, go along the box bottom a width w, then go upward along the other side h, and finally go w/2 along the box top back to the top center A. So the diagonal length of the wrapping paper D = w/2 + h + w + h + w/2 = 2(w+h). The area of a square equals half the square of its diagonal, so area = D^2/2 = [2(w+h)]^2/2 = 2(w+h)^2.
